dct_description_sm: Cirque glaciers in the Torngat Mountains of northern Labrador are the only glaciers on mainland Canada east of the Rocky Mountains and represent the southernmost limit of glaciers in the eastern Arctic.   Although relatively small in extent, these glaciers play an important role in local freshwater and marine ecosystems through meltwater inputs, related geomorphic processes and nutrient cycling.  Changes in the mass balance of these glaciers therefore will directly impact local ecosystem dynamics and integrity.  Apart from a brief monitoring period on four glaciers in the 1980s by Bob Rogerson , there has been no attempt to gauge the impact of changing climate on the volume and extent of the Torngat Mountain glaciers.   One goal of the Torngat Glacier project is to produce a digital database of all the glaciers in northern Labrador which can be used as a basis for quantifying glacier change and investigating relationships with climate change. The database is part of the Canadian contribution to the international Global Land Ice Measurements from Space (GLIMS) project, which is designed to monitor the world's glaciers primarily using data from optical satellite instruments (www.glims.org).  Another project goal is to establish a baseline of current glacier conditions to be used for ongoing monitoring, recent change detection and local hydrological assessment.
dct_title_s: Glaciers data in Northern Labrador (Torngat Mountains glaciers)
